| E2E-038 | GW6 | S2 | open | The migration's own list of V1 public resolvers puts **mainnet PublicResolverV4 `0xF29100983E058B709F3D539b0c765937B804AC15` under Sepolia** and leaves it out of mainnet (`packages/migration/src/contracts/knownResolvers.ts:16-34`). The address has code only on mainnet (14,512 bytes; none on Sepolia). On mainnet a name on V4 — the wrapper-aware resolver most wrapped names use — would therefore not count as a known public resolver: its resolver strategy degrades to `keep-v1` (no records read or replayed onto an owned PermissionedResolver), and for a **locked CANNOT_SET_RESOLVER** name the manager skips its PublicResolverSet membership check (`requiresPinnedPublicResolverMembership` needs `isKnownPublicResolver`), so the migration would go ahead and, if V4 were not certified, leave the name on a V1 resolver nobody can write to — without the refusal E2E-037 shows. Found by reading the list against the contracts-v2 deploy script, which certifies V3 `0x231b0Ee1…` and V4 for mainnet. Not reachable today: the manager's migration manifest is Sepolia-only. |

| E2E-037 | GW6 | S2 | open | A **locked V1 name with CANNOT_SET_RESOLVER burnt that sits on a V1 public resolver the migration controller does not certify cannot be migrated at all**, and the manager says only "The upgrade contracts don't match this account. Please contact support." The locked controller replaces the V1 resolver with PublicResolverV2 only when its `PublicResolverSet` includes it; the manager checks that first (`assertLockedPublicResolverSetMembership`, invariant `public-resolver-set-membership`) and blocks the upgrade when it does not — correctly, since the name's resolver can never change otherwise — but with a message that names neither the name nor the cause. **Sepolia:** the set includes the older public resolver `0xE99638b4…` but not `0x8FADE66B…` (ensjs `ensPublicResolver`, the one the apps and fixtures use): the deploy script approves "the single resolved v1 PublicResolver" (contracts-v2 `deploy/01_PublicResolverSet.ts`, branch `deploy/mainnet-v2-20261002`). **Mainnet (read 2026-10-19):** the set (`0xfFCe…bf62`, read through both the replaced controller `0xa19d…7BE6` and its 2026-10-18 replacement `0xc46b…694d`, whose PublicResolverV2 is now `0x66f9…a3e1`, no longer the `0x9Ca5…371f` the ticket names) includes **neither** PublicResolverV3 `0x231b0Ee1…` nor PublicResolverV4 `0xF2910098…`, which the same script lists for mainnet. The approvals are queued in the ENS DAO proposal for the 2026-10-18 replacement (contracts-v2 `contracts/deployments/mainnet/dao/calls.jsonl`, two `PublicResolverSet.approve(…, true)` calls; only the DAO timelock `0xFe89…44b7` holds `ROLE_APPROVE`), so mainnet needs re-checking once that proposal executes; until then every locked CSR mainnet name on those resolvers would be blocked the same way. Verified end to end on the local fork: on `0xE99638b4…` the name lands on PublicResolverV2 and its owner edits a record in the manager and the explorer (`migration-resolver.spec.ts` "certified"); on `0x8FADE66B…` the upgrade is refused ("current"). |

| E2E-032 | GS21 | S3 | open | A V1 **registry-only subname whose label the index does not know** is **silently left off** the upgrade list, and its parent migrates without it. `setSubnodeOwner` puts only the labelhash on chain (`NewOwner`), so bigname lists such a child as `[labelhash].parent.eth` unless its label reached it another way (an event carrying the name, or a rainbow-table import). How often production hits it depends on which labels the hosted bigname can name (its rainbow coverage was not checked); what happens to the left-behind subname's resolution once its parent is in V2 was not measured. Same rendering gap as E2E-020 and E2E-031, different reason. |

Measured 2026-10-14 on the local bigname (GS23): the subname resolves its text record and ETH address before the upgrade; after the locked parent migrates alone, both read back empty through the UniversalResolver, since resolution now walks the parent's V2 WrapperRegistry, which never received the subname. The V1 registry entry still exists, so the name is recoverable by re-creating it under the parent in V2, but nothing tells the owner. **Way out, verified (GS22):** wrap the subname and burn PARENT_CANNOT_CONTROL on it from the locked parent before upgrading; it is then a `detached-child` and migrates into the WrapperRegistry with its parent. | E2E-028 | GA10 | S3 | open | When a selected name's token **changes owner** between selection and confirmation, the upgrade stops with **"A permission is missing. Try again."** — the wrong reason, and an instruction that cannot work: the wallet no longer holds the name, so no retry or approval will migrate it. Likely mechanism: the transfer leaves the MigrationHelper unapproved for the new holder's token, so the simulation reverts `ERC721InsufficientApproval` before any owner check, and `decodeMigrationError` maps that to `permission-missing`. The app has the right copy ("One of your names changed owners. Refresh and select it again.", `token-owner-changed`) and does not reach it. Nothing moves on chain (the token stays with the new holder, V2 stays RESERVED). For contrast, an operator approval revoked behind the page ends correctly on "Your permissions changed. Go back to check the updated estimate." (unwrapped and wrapped). |
| E2E-027 | GW4 | S2 | open | A **desynced wrapped 2LD** — registrar lease live, NameWrapper expiry lapsed — **vanishes from its owner's upgrade flow**. It arises from a registrar-only renewal of a wrapped name — any renewal made through a legacy V1 controller rather than the NameWrapper, which is why ens-app-v3 models a `desynced` state and why `ETHRenewerV1` ships a separate `syncWrapper(labels)`. (Corrected 2026-10-11: the deployed `ETHRenewerV1` itself syncs the wrapper inline — traced, and pinned by B15 — so the manager's own V1 renewal does not create this state; names already desynced before launch still reach it.) Once the wrapper's old expiry (old registrar expiry + 90 days) passes, `NameWrapper.getData` reports owner 0 (PARENT_CANNOT_CONTROL is burnt on every wrapped .eth 2LD), bigname records the name as `active`, `wrapper_state: "lapsed"`, **owner and manager null**, and it is absent from the wallet's ENSv1 listing — so /upgrade never shows it, under any bucket. The name is recoverable (a `syncWrapper` restores the wrapper expiry, and with it the owner), but nothing in the manager calls or offers it (no `syncWrapper` anywhere in the app). Measured on the fork: registrar expiry > now, wrapper expiry < now, wrapper owner 0, V2 RESERVED at the renewed expiry; a control wrapped name beside it is listed. |
| E2E-026 | GM5 | S4 | open | A name that has **already migrated**, while the index still lists it as ENSv1, is dropped from /upgrade **without a word**. The selection is safe — it cannot be picked again (GU6 passes): the live preflight reads the chain and finds the V1 token gone. But the `already-migrated` ineligible reason exists in the enum (`classifyNames.ts:38-50`) and is never produced, `domain.isMigrated` is never read, and `getUnavailableNames` only renders `missing-registration` and `not-reserved`. A control name beside it is listed normally. Seen in practice only while the index lags the migration (a live local bigname flips the authority to ENSv2 within about a second), so the window is short. |
| E2E-025 | GS10 | S3 | open | An unlocked subname **wrapped under an unwrapped 2LD** (`NameWrapper.wrap`, which gives it no fuses and a wrapper expiry of **0**) is **silently left off** the upgrade list, and its parent migrates without it. Classification accepts it as a copy (`classifyNames.ts:416-423`: zero expiry without PARENT_CANNOT_CONTROL means "no independent expiry", deliberately not expired), but the live preflight drops it: `preflightChecks.ts` `isWrappedResultUnavailable` tests `expiry <= now` for copies with no such exemption, and `useEligibleV1Names` removes it from `eligible`. bigname lists the child correctly (owner = the wallet, wrapped, fuses 0, `wrapper_expires_at: null`, reason `not_set`). Nothing tells the owner. Likely second fault behind it: were it kept, the copy would pass `sourceExpiry = 0` to `UserRegistry.register`. A wrapped child with its own expiry under a wrapped 2LD is copied fine (GS3, and the 4-level chain in GS10). |
| E2E-024 | GR13 | S1 | open | Migration **silently drops every record when bigname has not yet listed the name's record keys**. The app learns which records exist only from bigname's key inventory (`seen_texts`, `seen_addresses`, `seen_singletons`, `seen_abis`; `v1ProfileKeys.ts`) and reads values on chain for those keys alone. An empty inventory is taken as "no records": no profile fetch, no replay, and the name still moves to the owner's new PermissionedResolver, so the V1 records stop resolving. It only fails safe (`ProfileFetchError`) when a name is missing from the lookup entirely, not when its key lists are empty. Measured on the local bigname (iteration 35): keys arrive **1.0–1.5 s after** the block is published and the name is listed, and a full-suite run hit the window (GR8 migrated with all four records lost). In production any indexer lag on the records projection opens the same window, and the loss is irreversible. |

The screen promises the opposite ("Your names, text records, and addresses will be carried over"). After the upgrade, measured through the UniversalResolver: `pubkey` **reverts** (the V2 PermissionedResolver has no pubkey record, so even a replay could not carry it) and `interfaceImplementer(0x12345678)` returns **zero**, though the V2 resolver does store interfaces (`InterfaceUpdated`) and the owner could have it replayed. A text record migrated beside them survives. Irreversible: the name has left V1. |

| E2E-019 | WEB-1572 test 1 (found verifying #1310) | S3 | open | After a registration completes, opening another name **in-app** (sidebar search, no reload) and pressing Register shows the **previous run** in the transaction modal: Submit commitment, Approve payment and Register name all "Done", each linking the first name's transaction, with Done in place of Start. Likely cause: `useRegistrationTransactions`' unmount cleanup returns early on `success`, the app navigates away after success without `handleDone`'s `clearTransaction()`, and `REGISTRATION_TX_IDS` are shared across names, so the next page's step list renders the old transactions. |

Reopening via **View registration progress** shows the landed deploy and commitment as "Not Started" with **Start**; pressing Start begins a new run, and the chain shows a **second** `deployProxy` and a **second** `commit` from the wallet for one registration (gas for a spare resolver and commitment; USDC is charged once). | E2E-016 | VK20 | S3 | open | The Token tab tells the owner of a **registry-only V1 subname** that their name is an **ERC-721 on the BaseRegistrar**, and shows a token id for it. It is neither. A subname held directly in the legacy registry has no token of any kind — the BaseRegistrar only ever holds `.eth` 2LDs — and the id shown is `labelhash(leaf label)`: for `l1.v1m-20-….eth` the page printed `14348782382986100785356643067205758148600308114560913711117973050161833687690`, which is exactly `cast keccak l1`. Measured on the fork: `BaseRegistrar.ownerOf` on that id **reverts** (no such token), and `nameExpires` returns 0. Register that 2LD and the subname’s Token tab starts pointing at a stranger’s NFT, with a contract address and id a holder could act on in an explorer or a marketplace. Source: `routes/$name/token.tsx` picks ERC-721 vs ERC-1155 purely on `getWrapperData` being null, then computes `labelhash(name.split('.')[0])`, which is only correct for a 2LD. | E2E-015 | VO7 | S4 | open | For a **wrapped** V1 2LD the Ownership tab renders a **Manager** row containing the **NameWrapper contract address** (`0x0635…FcE8`). Nobody holds that address: a wrapped name has one holder, the wrapper owner, and the legacy registry slot is the wrapper itself by construction. The row presents a contract as though it were an account a user could act as, on the page people read to find out who controls a name. ens-app-v3 — the app that owns V1 — deliberately renders no manager row for these names: `src/hooks/ownership/useRoles/utils/getRoles.ts:31-36` returns `owner` + `eth-record` for `eth-emancipated-2ld` and `eth-locked-2ld`, while the unwrapped 2LD arm above it does return a `manager`. Found by the V1 shape matrix (2026-09-13); measured on both wrapped shapes (emancipated and locked), and absent from the unwrapped ones, so it tracks wrap state rather than the viewer. |

| E2E-010 | F20 | S3 | open | `useTransferName`'s `set-eth-addr` step re-reads the name's **own** resolver at execution time specifically to catch the state changing under it — `queryClient.fetchQuery(getOwnResolverQueryOptions(...))`, then `throw new Error('${name} has no resolver of its own to update')`. The guard cannot fire. `apps/portal/src/utils/queryClient.ts` sets a global `staleTime: 1000 * 60 * 60`, so `fetchQuery` returns the value cached when the form rendered and never re-reads the chain. Its own comment — "a null here means the state changed underneath us; fail before touching the chain" — describes behaviour the app does not have: the step proceeds and writes `addr(60)` to whichever resolver was cached. Introduced with `getOwnResolver` in #1120, though the stale-cache interaction is the root cause rather than anything specific to subnames. **Scope**: harmless when the name's own resolver and its parent's are the same contract (the name inherits its way back to the resolver that was written), which is the shape the repro uses. It bites when they differ — the ordinary case, and the one `getOwnResolver` was added to distinguish — because the record then lands on a contract the name no longer references while the flow reports success. S3 not S2: the transfer itself still completes and nothing is destroyed; a records write is silently sent to the wrong place |
| E2E-008 | E1 | S3 | open | The indexer's `resolver.texts` (and presumably `.addresses`) field appears keyed by resolver **contract address alone**, not by `(address, node)`. Once two different names point their resolver slot at the same already-deployed resolver contract (`setResolver` — the resolver-level analogue of E2E-007's shared-registry pattern), each name's indexed text-key list bleeds into the other's, even though on-chain each node's records stay correctly scoped (verified directly: `text(nodeB, key)` reads empty on-chain while `domains(where:{name:B}).resolver.texts` reports the key). Confirmed deterministic once the indexer-sync race is handled (poll the writer's own domain until the new key appears before asserting on the other name) — an immediate, unwaited check on the reader can pass for the wrong reason |
| E2E-007 | D9 | S3 | open | A subname registered from a name's own `/subnames` page is misattributed to a *different* parent name, if that other name also points its subregistry at the same already-deployed registry contract (via "use a pre-existing registry contract" in `SubregistryConfigurator.tsx`). The indexer doesn't just misattribute the parent relation — it names the child domain entity using whichever name **currently** "owns" the shared registry pointer at index time (e.g. the entity is literally called `purple.kangaroo.eth`, never `purple.koala.eth`, even though `purple` was registered from `koala.eth`'s own `/create-subname` page): a single mutable registry → parent-name pointer, updated on `setSubregistry`, stamped onto every subsequent registration event from that registry regardless of which name's UI actually created it. Confirmed both when one wallet owns both names and when they are owned by two separate wallets (the latter needs an explicit `ROLE_REGISTRAR` grant to the second owner first, matching the Slack report). Mirror evidence also confirmed: the subname registered *before* the registry was shared stays correctly attributed to the original owner, and the second name's page shows both its own subname AND the misattributed one |
| E2E-003 | F14 | S2 | open | Retrying a transfer step whose wallet prompt was previously rejected deterministically fails — "Failed to submit transaction: An unknown RPC error occurred", every run, not intermittent |
| E2E-002 | F5 | S1 | open | Transfer to a non-receiver contract detaches the resolver irreversibly, then hangs — token never moves, no error shown |
